channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: Earthing & Grounding Systems Explained: Why Resistance Is the Whole Game
item.description: What an earthing system is actually protecting against, why grid resistance is the number that matters, the factors that drive it.

item.title: Earthing vs. Grounding: Same Earth Connection, Different Job
item.description: Earthing and grounding both connect to earth, but their purpose is different — earthing protects people from shock, grounding protects the electrical system. Purpose, connection point, current flow and where each is used, compared.

item.title: How to Calculate & Select Supply Air Terminal & Return Air Terminal
item.description: How to calculate supply and return air terminal quantity from room CFM — diffuser CFM/NC/throw selection, return grille face velocity, air balance, and a full worked example with layout.

item.title: Types of Earthing Systems: 9 Electrode Types Explained
item.description: Nine types of earthing electrodes explained — plate, pipe, rod, strip, wire, chemical, ring, mesh and equipment earthing — with what each is built from and where it's actually used.

item.title: BOD & BOP in Pipe Bending: The Key to Piping Take-Off & Fabrication
item.description: BOD (Bend Outside Diameter) and BOP (Bend Center Line) are the two dimensions that drive piping material take-off and fabrication. Formulas, a bend allowance table, and a worked 2-inch 90° bend example.

item.title: Types of HVAC Fans
item.description: The five main HVAC fan types compared — axial, centrifugal, inline, mixed-flow and exhaust fans. How each one works, typical applications and key advantages, so you can match the fan to the job.

item.title: FM-200 System Diagram: Components & How It Works Explained
item.description: FM-200 clean agent fire suppression system explained — cylinder, solenoid valve, nozzles, control panel, detection system, manual release station and pressure switch, with a full system diagram and how each part triggers discharge.

item.title: Gas Detector Types & Working Principles Explained
item.description: Catalytic bead, electrochemical, infrared, semiconductor and photoionization (PID) gas detectors compared — what each senses, how the sensing element actually works, and where each type is applied.

item.title: Sag in Transmission Lines Explained
item.description: What sag is in an overhead transmission line, why it's designed in rather than eliminated, the level-support sag formula, the factors that raise or lower it, typical sag-to-span ratios by voltage level, and why sag is checked at multiple temperatures.

item.title: UPS Architecture, Types & Operating Modes Explained
item.description: How an online double-conversion UPS is built — rectifier/charger, battery bank, inverter, static switch and bypass — the three operating modes, offline vs line-interactive vs online UPS types, and key protections and parameters.

item.title: Relay Basics: Construction, Working Principle & Contact Types
item.description: What a relay actually is, how the coil and armature switch a separate power circuit, NO/NC/CO contact types, a control-vs-power circuit diagram, common applications, key specs, and the trade-offs versus contactors and solid-state relays.

item.title: SCADA (Supervisory Control & Data Acquisition) Explained
item.description: How SCADA actually works — the field/communication/supervisory architecture, the 5-step monitor-to-action loop, components, communication protocols, SCADA system types, and SCADA vs DCS compared.

item.title: IEC 104 Communication Protocol Explained
item.description: What IEC 60870-5-104 actually does, how it extends IEC 101 over TCP/IP, the master-slave request/response and spontaneous-reporting model, a security reference, and where it's used in SCADA and remote control systems.

item.title: PLC vs DCS vs SCADA Explained: Real Industrial Comparison
item.description: PLC, DCS and SCADA compared for real industrial use — control type, speed, architecture, redundancy, and where control execution actually happens — plus a feature-by-feature table and typical applications for each.

item.title: 33/11 kV Substation: Single Line Diagram & Equipment Overview
item.description: How a 33/11 kV substation is built, walked through its single line diagram from incoming line to distribution feeders — every major equipment item, its function, and the protection schemes that back it up.

item.title: 4-20mA Current Loops: Why Industry Still Trusts an Analog Signal
item.description: Why 4-20mA beat 0-20mA and voltage signals for instrumentation, what live-zero actually protects against, how to convert a reading back to engineering units.

item.title: Essential Protection Settings of Air Circuit Breakers (ACB) Explained
item.description: LTPU, LTD, STPU, STD, instantaneous and ground fault settings on an Air Circuit Breaker (ACB) — what each protection parameter does, typical setting ranges, and why the settings exist as a coordinated set, not individual dials.

item.title: Access Control System (ACS) Explained: Components, Architecture & Site Work
item.description: How an Access Control System actually works — main components, the six-step credential-to-unlock sequence, system architecture, integration with FAS/BMS/CCTV, and what an electrical site engineer does on an ACS install.

item.title: AHU, FAHU, FCU, FMAHU, CSAHU: What Is the Difference?
item.description: What separates an AHU, FAHU, FCU, FMAHU and CSAHU — air source, installation style and typical application for each, in one comparison.

item.title: Air Changes per Hour: What ACH Actually Tells You (and Doesn't)
item.description: What air changes per hour (ACH) measures, the formula behind it, typical ACH targets by space type.

item.title: Alarm Setpoint Bands: Why High and High-High Are Different Alarms
item.description: Why alarms come in High/High-High and Low/Low-Low pairs, not single trip points, and how a reset deadband on each keeps the alarm list from flooding operators.

item.title: ANSI Relay Numbers: Common Protection Relay Functions
item.description: A working reference for the ANSI device numbers you'll actually run into on protection schemes — 50/51, 27/59, 87, 21, 67, 25 and more.

item.title: ATS, MTS, ECB & Switch Disconnectors: Transfer & Isolation Switching Devices Explained
item.description: ATS, MTS, COS, switch disconnectors, load break switches, fused switch disconnectors, ECBs, maintenance bypass switches and key interlocks — what each device does, how it differs, and where it's used.

item.title: Basics of Fire Protection in Buildings Explained
item.description: Passive protection, active systems, detection, suppression and safe evacuation — the five layers of building fire protection, how sprinklers, hydrants, fire pumps and alarm systems work together, and the simple working sequence from detection to fire brigade response.

item.title: Battery SoC vs DoD: Why They're Not the Same Number
item.description: Why SoC and DoD are two views of the same battery, how SoC is actually estimated in the field, and why chemistry sets the DoD limit that protects cycle life.

item.title: Beam Bending Basics: Why Section Modulus Decides Capacity, Not Just Load
item.description: Why a beam's bending capacity comes down to two separate checks — bending stress against section modulus, and deflection against span — not just the applied load.

item.title: Bearing Failures: Root Causes & Prevention
item.description: The five most common ways rolling-element bearings actually fail — spalling, lubrication breakdown, contamination, electrical erosion, and false brinelling.

item.title: Belt Drive Sizing: Why the Speed Ratio Alone Doesn't Tell You the Tension
item.description: Belt drive speed ratio, belt velocity and shaft torque from pulley diameters and power, and why tension depends on wrap angle and friction, not just geometry.

item.title: BMS Point Types Explained: AI, AO, BI, BO, MI, MO, BV, AV, MV
item.description: What each BMS point abbreviation actually means — AI, AO, BI, BO, MI, MO, BV, AV and MV.

item.title: Bolt Torque vs Preload: Why K-Factor Is the Number That Actually Matters
item.description: Bolt tightening torque from target preload using the short-form torque-tension relationship, and why the nut factor dominates the result far more than bolt grade.
